passage:
A new phone was advertised as easy to repair. Users could replace the battery, screen, and camera with simple tools.
Students compared it with phones that were difficult to open. They discussed why companies might design products that are hard to repair.
Some said sealed phones look better and resist water. Others said repairable products reduce waste and give users more control.
The class did not reach one perfect answer.
The phone became a lesson in design values. Every product chooses between priorities: beauty, durability, profit, repair, and convenience.
A device's shape tells a story about what its makers think matters.
